source_review.notes: Checked six official/primary sources. RFC 9111 supports cache keys, storage eligibility, freshness/age, stale restrictions, validators, revalidation, and HTTP invalidation. RFC 9110 supports selected representations, ETags, conditional requests, and precondition ordering. RFC 5861 supports bounded stale-while-revalidate/stale-if-error. RFC 9211 supports standardized Cache-Status. AWS supports hit-distribution, cold-start, local-fleet amplification, eventual-consistency, and coalescing guidance. Redis supports tracked client-cache invalidations and their bounded-resource tradeoffs.

evidence: Checked key k, versions v/v_i/v_f, generation/current time t_g/t, age A, freshness F, maximum staleness M, hit ratio h, request/origin rates lambda/lambda_o, fills C_f, instances I, and origin budget B_o for consistent scopes.
Confirmed freshness inequality differs from origin-state equivalence.
Confirmed version comparison assumes a defined total or causal order and safe epoch handling.
notation_and_syntax.notes: HTTP current-age calculation is delegated to RFC-compliant implementations rather than reduced to the explanatory application-cache equation.

evidence: Recomputed 20,000/s at 95% hits as 1,000 misses/s and full loss as 20-times steady miss load.
Recomputed 50,000/s at 98% hits as 1,000 misses/s and full loss as 50-times amplification.
Confirmed 1,000 callers across 50 locally coalescing instances can still yield up to 50 fills.
Checked age 45<60 freshness example, version 7<8 rejection, and exact ten examples/five answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Hit-ratio amplification calculations state their stable-mix assumptions and are not capacity guarantees.

evidence: Constructed two-request counterexample proving omitted authorization/representation dimensions invalidate key safety.
Constructed miss-read-v7/write-v8/invalidate-v8/late-fill-v7 schedule and confirmed high-water comparison prevents regression.
Derived cache-loss amplification lambda/((1-h)lambda)=1/(1-h) for h<1.
Confirmed one single-flight owner per process implies at most I fleet fills, not one.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Proofs list coverage, durable high-water, version comparability, and coordination scope assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed fresh/stale boundary, zero/long TTL, clock movement, invalid directives, weak/strong validators, 304 metadata, variants, partial/authenticated/private responses, and range/precondition distinction.
Reviewed miss/write/fill/delete races, duplicates, reorder, loss, gaps, reconnect, restore epoch, tombstone retention, multi-writer and multi-region cases.
Reviewed hot/cold/high-cardinality keys, negative/error cache classes, giant/compressed/mutable objects, eviction pollution, poisoning, tenant leakage, permission revocation, and sensitive metrics.
Reviewed synchronized expiry, local/fleet coalescing, cache slow/failure, origin slow/failure, cold deploy, autoscaling, invalidation storm, stale fallback, and gradual recovery.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage includes HTTP semantics, application coherence, security, concurrency, capacity, topology, and recovery.

evidence: Confirmed every representation/security-changing dimension participates in key or reuse eligibility.
Confirmed freshness, eviction, validation, invalidation, and domain validity remain distinct.
Confirmed no lower source version installs after a higher observed commit/invalidation version.
Confirmed invalidation follows commit through a durable/reconcilable path.
Confirmed fills/revalidation/fallback are bounded and write outcomes remain authoritative.
invariant_checking.notes: Cache failure never receives an automatic unlimited origin bypass.

evidence: Reviewed key-safety proof and confirmed one collision is a sufficient counterexample.
Reviewed version monotonicity and confirmed restart/epoch and uncovered-writer assumptions are explicit.
Reviewed miss amplification and confirmed request-mix/hit independence are labeled simplifications.
Reviewed coalescing scope and confirmed distributed coordination or origin budgets remain necessary.
proof_review.notes: No TTL, cache product, or invalidation mechanism is claimed to create strong consistency by itself.

evidence: Confirmed four arguments are labeled and separated from empirical load claims.
Confirmed HTTP directive/validator behavior is attributed to RFC 9110/9111/5861/9211.
Confirmed AWS and Redis mechanisms are scoped examples rather than universal cache protocols.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Normative protocol behavior, application design policy, and measured capacity obligations are distinct.

evidence: All six official/primary references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current guidance applies.
All rates, hit ratios, lifetimes, ages, instance counts, versions, and origin budgets are labeled scenarios.

Actual hit distribution, harm/staleness tolerance, key normalization, intermediary behavior, invalidation lag/loss, origin spare capacity, eviction, hot keys, and recovery remain explicit integration/load/fault evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production cache, CDN, origin, tenant set, or invalidation bus was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed storage/key/freshness/validation/invalidation, privacy, pattern choice, race prevention, reliable invalidation, stampedes, negative/error/stale caching, cache-loss capacity, eviction, observability, and verification as one coherence and capacity model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through key/reuse matrices, explicit directives, stable representation validators, versioned fills/high-water marks, outbox/change-log invalidation, reconciliation, per-key coalescing, origin budgets, bounded stale policy, capacity partitions, Cache-Status, and deterministic race/load tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module develops caching from independent protocol decisions through keys, freshness, validation, patterns, races/invalidation, stampedes/failure, capacity, and verification. Ten examples and five integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
